subject: Dedicated capacity: confirm GPU preference, throughput targets & $/1M token budget
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Torres <elena@heliopay.com>
Cc: Prioym Das <priyom@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated sizing & target $/1M token economics

Thanks for the call earlier — great to meet the HelioPay team. Summary and asks below so we can align on a concise dedicated proposal.

Quick recap (from our discovery):
- Workload: multi-turn financial assistant and reconciliation summarization. Typical convo length ~600-1,200 tokens (prompt+response).
- Traffic profile: steady-state ~30 concurrent inference sessions, peak spike windows around payroll runs (15-30 minute bursts) hitting ~700-900 rps/minute per microservice group.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 450ms for typical 512-token responses (want extra headroom for 1k+ token generation).
- Preferred isolation: Dedicated reservation behind VPC peering; procurement prefers fixed monthly commit.

Items we need from you to finalize a tailored SKU:
1) Target monthly token volume (range if uncertain) — e.g., 200M / 500M / 1B tokens per month.
2) Target unit economics: what target $/1M tokens would make a Reserved plan viable for HelioPay? (range is fine.)
3) GPU preference: H100, A100-80GB, or L40S/other? Any hard constraints from infra/security ops?
4) Typical max sequence length we should optimize for (prompt-only vs prompt+response).

What we propose next (action items from Redwood):
- I attached a preliminary estimate workbook with three configurations (conservative, recommended, aggressive) showing reserved GPU counts, burst options, and ballpark $/1M token math.
- Prioym and Marissa will sketch throughput targets by GPU type and include caching/quantization levers that impact unit costs.
- If the economics look good, we can put together a 60-day POC reservation and procurement template to speed approval.

Please reply with the three quick inputs above so we can lock numbers and send a formal quote.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
---

From: Elena Torres <elena@heliopay.com>

Cc: procurement@heliopay.com
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated sizing & target $/1M token economics

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and follow-ups below.

1) Monthly token volume: our internal baseline is ~450M tokens/month with anticipated 20-30% growth over the next 6 months. If we scope conservative commit, plan for 350M; comfortable discussing up to 750M for the committed term.
2) Target unit economics: procurement is pushing for $20–$25 per 1M tokens on a reserved plan. If we can get within that band given the needed latency/availability, we’ll move forward quickly.
3) GPU preference: infra prefers H100 for throughput and FP16 stability. They asked whether we support model variants that run efficiently on A100 if that materially drops cost.
4) Max seq length: plan for up to 1,024 tokens typical; occasional up to 2,048 for batch summarizations.

Concerns: burst handling during payroll spikes is critical — we need clarity on burst credits or short-term overprovisioning and how that impacts $/1M math. Also want an SLA commitment window for failover to a lower-cost model if capacity saturated.

Next step: procurement would like an estimated monthly invoice range and a sample SOW/invoice template for internal approval. Can your team prepare that?

-Elena
VP Product — HelioPay

Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated sizing & target $/1M token economics — proposed configs

Elena — thanks, great clarity on volume and GPU preference. I sketched three dedicated reservation options (summary below). Full math attached in the workbook.

Summary (ballpark, USD):
- Option A (Conservative): 2x H100 reserved + 1x burst H100 (on-demand)
  - Sustained throughput: ~180 tokens/sec sustained per H100 (model + 1k seq avg with batching)
  - Expected monthly capacity: ~320M tokens
  - Ballpark effective unit cost: $28–$32 per 1M tokens (includes SLAs and 24/7 support)

- Option B (Recommended): 4x H100 reserved + small burst pool
  - Sustained throughput: ~720 tokens/sec aggregate with better headroom for spikes
  - Expected monthly capacity: ~650M tokens (good fit for your 450M baseline + growth)
  - Ballpark effective unit cost: $18–$22 per 1M tokens (with prefix caching and KV cache for repeated contexts)

- Option C (Aggressive): 8x H100 reserved for heavy throughput needs
  - Capacity: 1.3B+ tokens/month; very low queuing and lowest marginal unit cost ~ $12–$16 per 1M tokens (requires larger commit)

Notes & levers that materially affect $/1M token:
- Prefix & KV cache utilization: can lower billable tokens by ~15-30% on dialog-heavy flows.
- Quantization and model choice: switching to a 4-bit quantized variant or smaller decoder checkpoints reduces per-token GPU cycles (we can run compatibility evals if you want).
- Autoscaling & burst: we can provision a small on-demand burst pool for payroll windows; billing for bursts is prorated and shows separately on the invoice.

Attachments: the workbook has a tab showing line-item pricing, invoice templates, and a sample POC SOW (60-day trial with reserved baseline).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) you’d like a formal quote for.
2) If Option B looks right, we’ll draft a one-page SOW + pricing table and a procurement invoice template.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical run-through with your infra team (H100 tuning, network peering, CPU buffer sizing).

I put conservative estimates in the sheet; Aisha can update the spreadsheet once we lock your exact token commit and burst profile.

— Prioym
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-estimate-helio-20260222.xlsx
